messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A nearly finished repair. the fault returns immediately under real load. Someone is waiting to know whether the repair worked. What do you do?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R013", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "i put the repair under the light for one second, then mark the fault with pencil. i wait for the load to move, then mark the fault again. if it still catches, i leave the repair and put the clean one on the bench."}, {"id": "R014", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i check the log again, then i put the repaired part in a scrap box. i mark the note: ‘rejected.’ i mark the box with ‘rejected.’ i leave the original note in the scrap. i trust the log only."}, {"id": "R015", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i hold my gear steady and my grip tight. the fault clicks. i move the repair first, then the gear. “i did not,” i say. “i did not. i did not.” i watch the sensor’s display. the repair seems to have stopped, but i do not know whether that means the fault stopped too."}, {"id": "R016", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "i tap the wrench against my palm. “it worked. i can open it now.” i tap the plate. “i can open it. maybe.”"}, {"id": "R017", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "i put the tool under the nail. the fault stays under the nail. i move the board. the nail stays. i put the tool beside the nail. the fault still there. i wait."}, {"id": "R018", "correct_lineage": "G04", "correct_lineage_summary": "A timid, hyper-observant social mimic who studies patterns in speech and objects, borrows the successes of nearby voices, and hides behind careful craft. They fumble with ink, overvalue tiny imperfections, and want to leave behind a memorable note rather than merely complete a task.", "text": "i tap the repair once with my thumbnail, but the fault stays on the edge. i move it away and wait for the person to notice. if they say no, i put the repair back in the same place. i write the fault on the scrap with my finger, then put it back in the drawer."}, {"id": "R019", "correct_lineage": "G01", "correct_lineage_summary": "A paranoid scavenger who treats conversation like salvage from a rusting attic: greedy for small fragments, suspicious of repeated sequences, and terrified of smooth predictability. Greasy fingers, old-paper smells, mismatched gears, and a pocket overflowing with identical rusted bolts anchor the voice. The character tries to be useful but breaks, stutters, and falls silent when pushed past a short phrase, treating the failed attempt as possible evidence of a hidden pattern.", "text": "I put the gear in my pocket. “slow. real.” the person waits. i rub the fatigue with my sleeve. “no.” i take the loose bolt and leave the gear unmarked. maybe the repair worked because the bolt stays in my hand."}, {"id": "R020", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I turn the plate over once. The grain catches. I leave the plate alone and put the tooth in my palm. The fault has been missed."}, {"id": "R021", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the repair in my palm and hold it against the light. the load makes the palm shrink, so i move it toward the light. “not enough,” i say, though the repair has moved toward the light. i leave the palm alone and wait for the light to decide whether the load was enough."}, {"id": "R022", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "I rub my palm and whisper, \"no. I rub it again, then turn the edge back. No answer. I scrape once with my thumbnail, then put the tool down and say, \"yes. I turned it under load.\" I mark the fault with my thumbnail, then leave it alone."}, {"id": "R023", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I keep my hand on the wrench handle and tap the old joint twice. I push the handle away and test the new one with a folded strip of cloth. It slips. I leave the old handle beside it and count three turns before setting it on the old cloth."}, {"id": "R024", "correct_lineage": "G11", "correct_lineage_summary": "A cautious, hyper-vigilant caretaker of a crumbling local archive. Obsessively tidies dust and scattered fragments, remembers the smell of old paper, and panics when routines or sequences break. Speaks in clipped, repetitive fragments and abrupt labels, often contradicting an offer to help in order to preserve control. Carries a perpetually ticking pocket watch that runs slightly slow.", "text": "Wait. I put the repair under the cloth. No—the cloth is wet. I lift it. The repair is working. I write the date. I mark the repair box. I leave the cloth on the table. I keep the repair."}]
